children: Williams to Discuss Exyn’s Physical AI Technology, Defense Applications and Participation in a U.S. Department of Energy Initiative to Advance Domestic Critical Mineral Discovery

-- Exyn Technologies (“Exyn” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: EXYN, EXYNW), a leader in physical AI for autonomous mapping and perception-driven navigation in complex, GPS-denied environments, today announced that Ben Williams, Interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Operating Officer, will appear live today on FOX Business Network’s Varney & Company at approximately 9:50 a.m. Eastern Time.

During the interview, Mr. Williams is expected to discuss Exyn’s physical AI technology, ExynAI®, and its growing applications across defense and national security, as well as the Company's participation, announced earlier today, in a national laboratory-led project selected by the U.S. Department of Energy (“DOE”) for award negotiations under its Mine of the Future Initiative.

Exyn is part of the national laboratory-led team supporting the Mining Autonomous Platform for Prospecting and Ore Discovery (“MAP-POD”) project, one of 17 national laboratory projects that DOE selected for a total of $29.5 million in funding under the initiative. Exyn is expected to contribute ExynAI-powered near-zero drift navigation for ground vehicle autonomy. According to DOE, the selected projects will reduce dependence on foreign supply chains, bolster national security and advance the technologies that will establish America’s long-term energy independence.

“We appreciate the opportunity to share Exyn's story with FOX Business viewers, particularly as our technology becomes increasingly relevant to some of the nation's most pressing priorities, including defense, national security and domestic critical mineral production,” said Ben Williams, Interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Operating Officer of Exyn Technologies. “Our role in this DOE-selected project reflects what ExynAI was built to do, which is to navigate and map underground and in other environments where there is no GPS and conditions can be hazardous for people. We believe these capabilities create significant opportunities to expand our technology across defense, critical infrastructure and other mission-critical applications.”
